title: Attestation Control Gaps & Telemetry Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is intended to guide security, infra, and compliance teams through a targeted readiness effort for auditor reviews (SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 annex mapping). It focuses on three technical pillars where we see the majority of evidence gaps: role-based access control (RBAC v2 rollout), application and infra telemetry (audit log schema), and automated evidence exports to the SIEM/evidence lake.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: platform control surface (API, console, dedicated control-plane components, private deployments) and downstream logging/export.
- Audience: security-and-compliance, platform-engineering, site-reliability-engineering, and solutions engineers preparing artifacts for auditors.

High-level control mapping summary (narrative):
- Purpose-built mapping: rather than a giant matrix, this doc maps specific technical capabilities to the control objective (detectability, availability, change control, access control). For each capability we list the authoritative evidence source, how we collect it, and the expected artifact for auditor review.
- Outcome: produce a short pack of 6–12 artifacts that an auditor can follow end-to-end (control description, live configuration, representative logs, export config, and sampling queries).

Key capability areas and authoritative evidence sources:
1) RBAC v2 (policy model + enforcement)
   - Evidence sources: IAM policy store snapshot (git history), live policy bindings from control plane, enforcement audit traces from API gateway, sample access review reports.
   - How we collect: nightly policy export job (json), weekly snapshot to evidence-bucket, on-demand exports for auditor sessions.
   - Auditor artifact: policy snapshot file + console screenshots showing binding for sample user + trace showing denied/allowed decision for test user.

2) Audit log schema & retention
   - Evidence sources: event streams (app-audit, infra-audit, control-plane-audit), schema registry entries, retention policy in logging config, S3 retention lifecycle policies, and SIEM index mappings.
   - How we collect: schema.json stored in repo + example NDJSON log samples (one file per week) + retention policy doc.
   - Auditor artifact: schema definition, a 1-week log sample for a control-relevant event, and a retention policy screenshot (console/terraform).

3) SIEM export & evidence automation
   - Evidence sources: export connector configs, uptime/transfer logs (delivery success/failure), automated snapshots delivered to the evidence-bucket, alerting rules linked to compliance monitors.
   - How we collect: periodic export validation job that generates a signed manifest (sha256) for each upload.
   - Auditor artifact: manifest for a sample period, transfer logs showing successful delivery, and a diagram of the export pipeline.

Concise gap analysis (observations and impact):
- Finding A: inconsistent event fields across services (e.g., some services log user_display_name but not user_id).
  - Impact: difficult to correlate identity across events for access review; increases manual evidence curation.
  - Short remediation: adopt minimal canonical fields (principal_id, principal_type, action, resource, outcome, timestamp, request_id) and enforce via schema registry.

- Finding B: RBAC drift between git snapshot and live bindings due to emergency changes made via console.
  - Impact: policy snapshot may not match live enforcement during audit sampling.
  - Short remediation: require PR for any console change within 24h or run an automated nightly reconciliation job and surface diffs.

- Finding C: SIEM export failures occasionally reattempt without documented retry policy visible to auditors.
  - Impact: auditors may view missing data windows as noncompliant.
  - Short remediation: formalize retry policy, capture transfer metrics, and include retry behavior in evidence manifests.

Technical evidence checklist (what to prepare for an auditor walk-through):
- For RBAC: git history snapshot (last 30 days), live binding list for 3 sample services, sample allow/deny decision trace, and proof of review for role changes (PR links).
- For telemetry: JSON schema file, sample NDJSON logs covering at least 7 days, retention policy doc, and SIEM index/mapping screenshot.
- For exports: connector config, signed manifest for sampled upload, transfer logs (with request_id), and failure/retry audit.

SIEM export and parser readiness (operational play):
- Standard export format: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), compressed with gzip, filename pattern: service/year=YYYY/month=MM/day=DD/part-N.ndjson.gz. Each file must include first-line metadata header with: export_id, start_ts, end_ts, sha256, schema_version.
- Required canonical event fields (enforce across services): principal_id, principal_type, action, resource, resource_type, outcome (success/failure), timestamp (ISO8601), request_id, service_name, host_id, ip_address, user_agent (optional).
- Parser checklist for SIEM: field mappings, timestamp parsing, request_id map for session stitching, and identity enrichment via lookup table.

Sample event (single-line NDJSON example):
{"export_id":"exp-20260225-01","start_ts":"2026-02-25T00:00:00Z","end_ts":"2026-02-25T00:15:00Z","schema_version":"v2.1","events":[{"timestamp":"2026-02-25T00:02:17Z","service_name":"control-plane","principal_id":"usr_1234","principal_type":"user","action":"bind_role","resource":"project:alpha","resource_type":"project","outcome":"success","request_id":"req-5a2d","host_id":"cp-01","ip_address":"34.72.1.23"}]}

Note: for auditor samples we prefer flattened single events (one JSON object per line) rather than embedding arrays; the above is a compact example for engineering.

Suggested remediation roadmap (3-month horizon):
- Week 1–2: finalize canonical schema v2.1 and release schema registry policy. Owner: Ethan Wu. Deliverable: schema.json and enforcement linter in CI.
- Week 3–4: implement nightly RBAC reconciliation job and automated diff notifier. Owner: Marta Svensson. Deliverable: reconciler Lambda + dashboard.
- Month 2: implement export manifest signer and retention policy proof-of-config in terraform. Owner: Diego Alvarez. Deliverable: signed-manifest process + terraform doc.
- Month 3: prepare auditor artifact pack and run internal dry-run with compliance team. Owner: Priya Natarajan. Deliverable: artifact zip + walkthrough script.

Auditor Q&A prep (sample questions and suggested evidence):
Q: How do you ensure the correctness of role assignments when changes occur via the console?
A: Show the nightly reconciliation diff (S3 object) and a PR that caused the console change; show the policy snapshot and the reconciliation alert ticket.

Q: Can you demonstrate a representative access denial and how it is logged?
A: Provide an API gateway trace for the denied request, the flattened NDJSON log line, and the SIEM alert rule that would surface this as an incident.

Q: How do you prove exported logs were delivered intact to the evidence-bucket?
A: Provide the signed manifest, the checksum, transfer logs from the export job, and the S3 object metadata showing the uploaded file (size, etag).

Packaging and delivery recommendations for audit sessions:
- Create a small artifact repository with 8–12 items: control summary, policy snapshots (rbac), schema.json, 7-day log sample (flattened), export manifest, reconciliation diff, transfer logs, and a README describing how to verify checksums.
- Include a short walkthrough script (5–7 mins) for each artifact explaining what the auditor should validate.

Open issues for follow-up:
- Consent and PII handling for log samples (anonymize principal_id before handing to auditors unless NDA scope allows raw identifiers).
- Finalize retention language for immature regional exports (APAC regions have different S3 lifecycle defaults).
- Flag for Architecture: add request_id propagation for a specific legacy service (svc-legacy-bridge) to complete end-to-end traceability.

Appendix: quick references
- Canonical fields checklist (copy to be included with schema.json).
- Minimal auditor artifact list (1-page PDF template).
- Contact list for session: Priya Natarajan (owner), Ethan Wu (telemetry lead), Marta Svensson (IAM/RBAC), Diego Alvarez (exports).

End of playbook.
